Maternal exposure to secondhand smoke (SHS) during pregnancy
outcome: Risk of cerebral palsy (CP) in children
cohort: Mother-child pairs (n=5067) from Shandong Province, China
finding: Maternal exposure to secondhand smoke during pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of cerebral palsy in children, with a dose-response relationship observed with increasing exposure duration.
mod_finding: While controlling for delivery mode, this study found that maternal exposure to secondhand smoke during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of cerebral palsy in children.
followup_time: Until diagnosis of CP or end of study
birth_weight: Measured and included as a confounder in the analysis
